subject: Transportation Systems
title: Car-Free City Centers
description: A 60-second lesson on Car-Free City Centers.

hook.text: Oslo removed nearly all parking spots from its city center. Businesses thrived, not suffered.

buildup.text: Car-free zones give streets back to pedestrians, cyclists, and outdoor dining. Air quality improves.

discovery.text: Barcelona's superblocks close interior streets to through-traffic, creating mini-neighborhoods.

twist.text: Shopkeepers always oppose car bans—then sales usually rise as foot traffic replaces car traffic.

climax.text: Paris, Milan, and Brussels are all expanding car-free zones. The trend is accelerating post-Covid.

punchline.text: Remove the cars, and the city comes alive.

quiz.question: What typically happens to retail sales in car-free zones?
options: They usually rise as foot traffic increases
